title: Mochin DeTzelem, Vol. 11: The First Facts
subtitle: Being, difference, relationship and pattern: the ground of a Torah systems theory.
html:
From Mikraei Kodesh, the Torah writings collected on liorsollyshachar.com.

1. The first fact is that there is Being, not a void. Anything that exists, or anything we can say about it, comes after this primal fact of undifferentiated isness. This must be the beginning of Systems Theory1.

2. The second fact is that there is difference; there is two. The heterogeneity of what exists is not a contradiction to its unity. Colors differ, yet all are wavelengths of light. There are states of matter, yet they are all states of the same substance. There are many words, but all are equally arrangements of language. Similarly, particular instances of existence are bound and unified by being arrangements of Being itself; you can never get beyond Being as we exist within it. And yet, there are things. Things are discrete entities which populate a space of Being, because a thing implies at least two: the entity with its boundaries, and that which lies beyond, the space in which it exists. Space is context, space is the room in which a thing can be. So once again, the second fact is that discrete things populate the space of being.

3. The third fact is that things are not static, solitary entities; they relate to one another. Relationship involves at least three: two things, plus the connecting relation itself, often purely informational, yet observably manifest. So, we have (1) the unified Being that is, (2) a thing in the space of Being, and (3) the relationship between things. This is what begins to demand systems theory2, but only partially.

4. Random interactions alone cannot give rise to systems. We need a fourth fact, that pattern is the ground for emergence. Pattern integrates things into a structure; pattern is logic itself. Without cohesion and coherence throughout the things in Being, a shared meaning in what relationship implies about behavior and identity, there would be only the most basic elements knocking about in chaos, or worse, the total void of non-relation. But we do not live in such chaos; we live in a patterned world. Within a space where things relate to one another emerging in unity, elements and relationships can coalesce into systems. A system is now an entity we can observe as having its own identity and its own relationship to other things and systems.

5. Terminology. Things, elements — these are nodes3. Nodality is more robust than the import of ‘individuality’: it is the quality by which something defines its inside and outside, self and other, because such things are the necessary anatomy of a node, the systemicity of a system. Nodality recognizes that things are embedded in systems, bound up with Being itself. Nodality is always relational, but once manifest, its identity4 is ontologically real: it is a discrete, self-sufficient manifestation of Being in itself as much as it is defined in contrast to what lies beyond it. Identity is always dual, what the thing is alone, i.e., its real integral existence, its anatomy, and also its name, which is who the system is in relation to the one connected with the system via that name. The name is defined in relation, while the anatomy preexists. A name does have real effects though, because it mediates and morphs the topology of the relationship between the two nodes. With that understanding we can compose the following sentence: A system is an entity composed of Nodes and Relationships, made of and existing within the total space of Being, differentiated as an individual identity by boundaries between it and the environment beyond, and capable of relating as a whole (i.e. a Node) to other things and systems.

6. A system is never bare and one dimensional, it is immediately composed of a thick flesh, an inside and an epidermal surface, an interface with the world. An interface is always three. You must have an interface to go between two extremities, and thus, the interface is the relational medium that allows extremities to make contact. This interfacial layer is the site where the system’s inside (self) and outside (environment) meet through a medium that shapes what may pass. Mediation is the universal condition of relation between systems. The medium is the topology of the system’s subjective account of external experience5. All contact with outside the system is patterned by the logic of the medium itself. In other words, the medium is not a passive membrane or even exclusively the determinant of how.

Medial layers actively participate in the shaping of exchange, conditioning what the system can take in and what it can express, in addition of course to How Much. In this sense, mediation is both a constraint and a horizon of possibility6, preserving the system’s identity while enabling it to participate in larger ecosystems of relation. Without mediation, inside and outside would collapse into one another, and the system would dissolve into undifferentiated Being. The precondition for relationship is clarified boundaries of identity.

7. Nodes, Relationships, Systems - those are all nouns. Nouns are static, Behavior is a verb. The axis of time are the turn-by-turn snapshots7 of every thing’s position in the relational space of all things in a given moment, and as you string those moments together, you observe behavior. A system’s flesh does two things: receive inflow information and express outflow information. All behavior is an aspect of outflow8. To understand something, you must consider its behavior, its verb-history, just as you consider its noun-structure.

8. A system’s behavior is a traversal in decision space (or if the system is dead, then through inert possibility space). Decision is the assertion of one path over all others, collapsing the cloud of possible futures into a single actuality. Each decision sets constraints for the subsequent world that system steps into, warping the space in which all subsequent behavior unfolds. Inflow opens and shapes the possibility space; outflow is the realized choice. Yet the decisions of a system do not always follow deterministically from the inflow. The particular Inflow may gesture toward a decision (which is what late-stage capitalistic commodity advertising is founded on). In many systems though, a new matrix for choice — more than the sum of the nodes and carrying irreducible novelty — emerges for the system to travel in as its new higher order self. This new system turns inflow into outflow that reshapes the world around it in ways a complete history of inflow could never have foretold, exerting a downward causation from the new corpus of desire that didn’t exist in the environment beforehand. Behavior is never deterministic (unlike how advertising agencies think of living organisms other than themselves). There may be pattern in these decisions, nay there must be pattern, but never determination. The entire history of past decisions might have carved out a neural trough with repetition that might be hard to get out of, but what one was a second ago doesn’t need to have any relationship to one’s freedom now in this new moment9. Decision is always already the condition of behavior, necessarily forcing significance into behavior at any level.

9. Narrative is the meaningful integration of behavior across time, the ultimate pattern. Narrative is an even more ethereally informational layer of Being than the nouns and verbs which form its body. Even the object of ‘relationship’ is more concrete in comparison because narrative cannot impose itself on the systems that compose it. Narrative is the written product of systems actions over time, often emerging without the protagonist awareness within the narrating systems themselves. Narratives form carry forward the macrostructure of the past. And though the main causal vectors in system space are the microbehaviors acting on any given system in particular, Narrative is a real thing, the form in which the past is integrated into the present such that meaning endures.

10. You will nearly always find the duality between two systems where one is the body and the other is its Blood. Blood is a liquid, it flows through the system in a current, but that currency is usually composed of blood cells, a quantized, discrete, atomic unit that in aggregate forms the bloody liquid of a systems stock10. When we look at inflow and outflow, we are looking at the blood coursing through a system; all currency is blood. Desire is the blood of behavior, attention is the blood of love, and a blood transfusion from one with the ability to pay more attention into the eyes of one who hasn’t been looked at like a human being worthy of attention as far back as they can remember might just save their life. The cells of society’s blood are communications. A single word, picture, or twitch of body language is a token of communication. Blood is always a delivery. So tokenized value units, i.e., money, is the blood flow of economic communication and valuation11. Biosemiotics tries to find the matrix of tokenized meaning in animal communication, but even that enterprise is but a small interest in the grand project of biological understanding on the whole; every biological system is always communicating the blood of information even within itself, electricity through the nerves, endocrine signaling, signals along the gut brain axis, the list goes on. All communication is blood flow, and communication of information is the foundation of biological integrity and interrelation; interrelation because all relationship happens through the blood flow of communication across an interface. Thus, blood always passes by way of the number three12, the interface. Our bodies within themselves are always expressing token of information, through endocrine signaling, nervous signaling, perhaps along the Gut-Brain axis. What flows is the dimension of communication tokens. Notice how these objects differ from systems the systems themselves. Oftentimes, these tokens are systems themselves, perhaps made of paper, sound or hormones, but always far simpler than the systems in which they flow. If you look at a random cell in the body, it is its own system, doing its own thing. Money doesn’t seem to be doing its own thing, its only meaningful because it flows as blood through much larger, more complex systems.

11. In any system, we can observe a polarity: life and death. These are broad themes that look different in different places, but they recur wherever systems appear. To identify something as a system is, in effect, to say it is alive. Here “alive” is not borrowed from biology because biology is the borrower from a state that is already defined in the heights of abstraction, before biology was even a thought. Life is the assertion of patterned coherence and cohesive, nodal identity over chaotic entropy13, of which biological organisms are one local instance. Sand on a beach is not a system; the grains are merely in proximity, with no relationship. When the cells of an animal interrelate to form an organism, taking in resources and acting in co-ordination toward self-directed goals, we observe life. In the event of that animal death, the central coordination is lost, subsystems for information exchange and resource processing break down, and its parts dis-integrate, i.e., the sans-system state becomes the death of a system identity even though those parts become reabsorbed into Being elsewhere. Stepping in to a higher frame, the universe itself is alive by the same metrics of pattern, relation, and persistence that identify life anywhere. Life on Earth surpasses the inert mechanics of galaxies in the density and complexity of its structure by orders of magnitude. Nothing out there is as interesting as what’s right here, and as people are fond of pointing out, the brain is the most complex structure in the known universe. But is not the life on earth part of a bigger whole, a single animal that is the universe entire?

12. With systems theory, the question “Why does this work?” becomes “What does the system want14, and how does that shape its relationships and the nodes it contains?” The central component of a nodal identity is the want-cluster that looks like a teleology. A system has a coherent aim, often simply to persist in its existence and perhaps to grow, both goals which are constrained by the finitude of its environment producing constraints in its structure, boundaries and communication. Desire is the engine of life and the energy of telos; it is the organizing drive that bends relationships and flows toward the system’s continuity and expression. We can then ask what health means for a system, and what patterns might signal its unsustainability. We can identify universal principles of construction that solve problems which get in the way of any desire a system may have and thus move across disciplines, allowing analogies and solutions to pass between domains once thought unrelated.

13. Power is the capacity of a system to actualize its desire within the constraints of its environment. Power extends beyond the context of e.g. human political dominance. Power is the abstract measure of a system’s ability to shape the flows and information in itself and its environment, either in maintaining its boundaries in the fight for existential persistence, or in furthering its quest for growth. Power is neither inherently good nor bad. It is the degree to which a system can do in the world. We might evaluate the use power in terms of its relationship to adjacent systems in the environment, and we might consider some models of power to be manipulative and extractive, but even those are just factual observations clean of moral import. If a system is ‘good’ or ‘bad’ depends wholly on your perspective. One disease’s health is another system’s death.

14. Systems relate to other systems. They exist nested across scales, on one level a node within a larger system and on another level composed of nodes that are themselves systems. Across scales, emergent identity flows upward and constraints press downward, so that each system’s identity is both the product of its own coherence and the field of an environment of systems in which it lives. From such a perspective, one can consider the entire universe to be one massive, mythical animal15 where all the systems we look up at are subsystems, because by definition they are, all the way up to the highest most inclusive circumferential system. Resources of any kind – informational, energetic, material – are a subsystem, defined as such by a higher scale of systems that treat ‘resource’ systems as their content. Systems integrated with one another are in a constant symbiosis, shaping one another’s form in co-ordination.

15. Among the systems that originated on Earth are biological systems, and within these, Human systems. Human systems are the most complex of these because human nodality is distinguished by a symbol-mediated16 consciousness. The human experience of the world is the realm of the Adjective. In systems terms, the Adjective is the moment when nouns and verbs are disclosed to human nodality as quality-bearing, possessed of value, feeling, and significance.

16. Consciousness maps new dimensions onto the world, such as value and meaning. The human world is first a mental model and then a lived experience. On one level, a person’s experience has a climate defined the macromodel of their world. But varying within that space is the weather, or one’s particular contextual state The intersection of those two layers of individual human Being (being hungry, ugly, the Prime Minister or all three) filter perception so that all information, objects and experience alike, are perceived and experienced in a certain way. We live in these spaces before we live in a shared world, and they determine what, not just how, in the world is seen.

17. Human consciousness consumes the entire world as data within the structure of a continuously developing memory. It is that memory which nurses17 an inner rendering of the entire world, a ‘macromodel’. In such a feedback structure, particular moments are never the total space, they are but a particular space that is really just an example of what the world is as a whole, and when the world as experienced locally doesn’t accord with ones expectation of what the world aught to be like, the experience of that might be frustrating is one is unwilling to update their model of what the world is in reality.

18. Of the forms of inner worldbuilding that take place within the Human mind is narrative. Narrative is the gestational space of one’s inner world; within it, data digestion takes place and is embedded in the mnemonic web past experience; perception is ordered and mapped, value is assigned, and the moment is written in a history that transcends the locality of the particular. The womb of narrative generates a world of narrative meaning that shapes our actions. Decision space is now polarized with the valence narrative space.

19. ‘Philosophy18’ is an example of a Human system with the classic inflow and outflow. Its inflow is the world data it selects as important, and its product is the ordered structure it generates. It digests, gestates, and births experience, assembling nodes and relationships into an world. When it stays close to the prerogative of truth, philosophy forms the understood reality toward greater alignment with the true reality, in whatever dimensions it considers important. Science asserts itself as the strictest philosophy, but from physics to continental speculation, the root is one: migration toward a worldspace more coherent and more alive than the world of yesterday we thought we lived in.

20. Philosophy is always situated within the person. It cannot be separated from the conditions into which a person is born, i.e. the world already present before their first thought. Every philosophy is shaped by the corporeal vantage through which it is lived, and every act of thought is bound to the lived world of the thinker. While philosophy attempts to construct the world beyond the particulars of one’s given subset of sense experience available, being that one’s sense of the world by default feels itself to encompass the whole world rather than one’s own world, there remains a boundary on what the experienced world can possibly disclose about the whole world19. In other words, philosophy is not a view from nowhere; it is a subsystem nested within the person’s own life.

21. The lovely feature of our species-wide pursuit of truth is the collaboration of all our vantages throughout history through the symbolic media that shapeshift in the various forms of the world. In this way, a conversation refining certain worldviews can persist for generations, living within the lineage of people who make themselves the chariot for the prehension of certain genealogies of thought, each picking up where the last generation left off. A total experience of systems theory20 can only be the result of prehending vastly divergent worlds in the multiverse of human thought, and committing to the implications of recognizing their common boundary: they exist in the same universe. All thought in any direction is joined by the penetrative vector pointing towards the same reality, driving the same migration of experience toward the space of truth. At the foot of the forest all are unified in purpose, but diverge into groups, all slashing away with their machetes through different paths in the thickets of obscurity. The eventual convergence on similar ground at the end, and the interoperability of knowledge gained within their respective paths, point to a commonality of territory that vastly outweighs any observation of distinction within the pathways. The world is thus disclosed over time to be really of one structure, of one substance. This is of course a result of our first fact. And yet a true systems theory must break wide portals of potential for utterly individual human worlds and experiences, and it must hydrate a motivation towards personal worlds that can coexist complementarily in the cottage industry of the human multiverse. This is of course a result of our second fact. As above stated, clear boundaries of identity is what makes intimacy and relationship possible. Once we fully feel what it’s like to be us and in our world, consider how the beauty of living compounds exponentially when our eyes open to the kaleidoscopic novelty of life as experienced by the Other! This is of course a result of our third fact.

Notes

  1. Systems theory means simply that everything is a Havaya Achat.
  2. Now we need Torat Atzilut to do the work of telling us there is only one, and what that relationship is.
  3. There is a very high olam even before we even have the Olamot HaMalbush, and way before our Ak (which according to the ??? may in fact be the fourth Ak). It is the space where Otiot form from the beginning. The formation of those otiot begin with nodes, simple points of Rachamim, that float around as the Ohr of the Tas in that olam retreats. These points are then joined by relations, lines, which form the letters. Letters are the atoms of the shemot we see, but they are molecules of subatomic arrangements of Rachamim and Dinim, each one its own patterned structure of those two simple energies. Every atomic Kli (i.e., Ot) is composed of a Yud, a Dot (which is a circle, a complete system with ten inside, Yud begematria Ten) and a connection, a Vav, that is mechaber the points together. This is why all the otiot begin with a point, a yud, and extend from the yud into whatever that energtic arrangement is going to form. Every time you see a line, or a Kli in general, you have Seter, Rosh Toch Sof, which is three points and two lines between them. The Yotzer Meorot makes keein this diagram. To clarify, this isn’t kelim as we know them, because those are a much thicker phenomenon showing up in Atzilut which is the ikar makom of the Otiot and Shemot. But understand a shimmer of the implications of this origin story of kelim that chachamim were megale! First of all, this that were discussing in very sanitized natural language, reconstructing the footing under our feet with the simple observation of nodes and relations as two instances of heterogeneity in what is still an undifferentiated sea of Being as it were, is all really an observation of the root phenomenon. The root of our bria is two, the Bet of Bereshit, and these dualities will keep showing up. But as we’ve said in point three, you never have two because two means three, and it’s the relationships between two and the space that brings them together that makes two mean anything. The most immediate integration of this story is in whats called blackboxing. There is a term in engineering where we could accept that there us underlying complexity but we don’t need to actually deal with it, meaning, I know these inputs equal those outputs and I can operate with that level of understanding, ‘what,’ without needing the answer to ‘how.’ We can [bracket] things that we see, and only engage with the higher order epiphenomenon of their singularity. Meaning to say, a chemist doesn’t need to know anything about quantum mechanics which is why they can still think about the periodic table with the Rutherford model of the atom because the fact that Rutherford was wrong is an insight in how, not what atoms do when we are trying to make medicine for example. You look at a chair and see one thing. It is composed of many things, but there is a dimension in which it is one. So you can clarify the way you see the world by understanding that all the things you see are a Yud, a single whole point, even though that any whole is begematria ten and has all the anatomy of any given system within it. But you can then notice that two Yuds have a relationship to one another, and you can interrogate the dimension of Vav, what is the nature of that relationship. So there are two container spaces of information that can be dealt with separately, and with those you can make sense of most anything in the world. The challenge begins when you need to identify what set of Yuds in the infinity of Yuds that exist do you want to study, because there are many sets. There is [all the pieces of Art], there is the climate data for all the continents during the Jurassic period, there is a set of dvarim sheein lahem shiur, there is what your neighbor had for lunch, what they plan to have for dinner, and what that might indicate to the cerebrally inclined yenta as to how their intervening day was spent. When you hold a math textbook in your hand, that’s a Yud. You unpackage it to some random page and you see words on a page, and now you are within the subsystem of that systems content. You take it line by line, what is each line saying, how does it relate to the previous lines, notwithstanding the preliminary stage of looking at each word and how it relates to the others within the system of the sentence. That thought object that emerges at the end is itself the Yud you are trying to grasp, which is the whole reason that the material Yud as it were was composed in a printing shop to begin with! You need to bring very different ocular frameworks when you want to metabolize the information contained in book of differential calculus versus when you want to psychoanalyze the neighbors. Psychoanalysis is itself a new form of Kli developed, theoretically, to break apart the discrete Yud of the subconscious and translate its raw form in terms of some interpretive language. So, in sum, always approach the world with an understanding of those questions that will snipe at the best information directly, what are the Yuds, what are the Vavs, and what do you want to know about them.
  4. In this sense, we arrive at ‘Nodality’ as a sanitized veil on the term Yesh, which is identity, which is the alterity of Kelim, a Yesh meAyin, the identity revealed in Kav Emtzai besod Ze Moshe HaIsh, Ish besod Mochin Degadlut. Yesh is a thing, the thingness of a thing. Bitul hayesh is the dissolution of thingness in the face of singularity that has no room for true separation. Yesh is always a bubble. A system is always a bubble. Doesn’t that sort of sound like you are a bubble, in that you are a yesh, a system of otiot, which is an identity, a thing in existence, given existence as an alterity within Havaya, i.e., Being?
  5. Too often it is the case that one’s access to reality, in reaction to which one has emotions and makes logically concluded decisions, is only from a report of reality, and that report is not itself reality. Always peak your ears to notice when a report is being added to bare facts, and what facts are or are not being included in the report. This applies, most of all, to your own perception. We can all see the gaps in other peoples thinking, that isn’t wisdom.
  6. In other words, a levush is always a helem, but also an olam. This is the secret of the first time we find Nukvah showing up is in the Daled separated from the Vav in the Chalon of Chotem. The Ari says in Otzrot on that Daled that it is actualy a composite of the two middle level teamim, the pasek and the makef. The pasek is the virtical line | that tells you stop, Pasek as in Psak which is metzamtzem the Ohr in pratei dinim so we can make kelim for it here. But while its Pasek, it allows Makef, the – that tells you to be mamshich to the next word. Or succinctly, Malchut is always both a contraction and a dilation of something new.
  7. As alluded to in the past, the secret of time is not a physical phenomenon. It is a clockwork of shemot in which everything that exists (which are by definition shemot) is re-rendered in world of that new time which is a new shem (i.e. a new Ratzon that is invoked by that shem in terms of that shem).
  8. For example, someone might buy something, which is both a behavior and an inflow, and then use it, which is an outflow. Or an atom might receive the information that there is another atom nearby that hungers for an electric charge and so they snap into a covalent bond. You have expressed an internal impulse to do something to outside, to bring yourself into the outside through the interface of your body.
  9. Every past moment will exist unchanging in its place within being. The sediment you think has accumulated with time is nonexistent. You are always free to slip out of an old world and into a new one like a snake from its skin and renew your approach to what the universe is and what you want to do within it. Nothing is weighing on you to be the person you were a second ago, and every moment is as free as any other moment. There is no real pit that you can’t get out of because time isn’t a shovel that digs deeper into a particular reality, it is a straight ground that at any point you can teleport to a new territory on that ground and live the way you want to. Are there going to be practical challenges that do manifest as the sedimentary layers of past decisions? Sure, but that is not something that should bend what you want to be and who you decide to become. The moment you want, you are a new person, notwithstanding that you are forced to clean up the mess a previous iteration of you made assuming you would be the one cleaning up. Paying the debts that your past self took out on your current self shouldn’t force you to identify with that old self just because you are the one getting stuck with the bill.
  10. Call them tokens or parcels or what have you, the domain specific terminology is immaterial. The emergence of discrete tokenized units of meaning from a continuous substrate is the essence of how the shemot in the olamot elyonim recruit olam haze in discrete material systems that enbubble their boundaries. That pattern is a deeply enchanting thing to look at, that the world is in essence continuous, but then discrete, and that discrete world enters into the continuous substrate of Golem Nekevah and makes an emergent discretion once again.
  11. Hence ‘Damim.’ Money is just the crystalized blood cells of fiscal shefa. All blood is shefa, ki hadam hu hanefesh. You have energy to move? You have social capital amongst your friends? You have legs with the ability to go however many miles per hour before sitting? You have blood. The capitalist system would want you to believe that money is crystalized labor, but that often isn’t the case. Its something else, but you can certainly try and translate your labor into interoperable currency that can act as a valid communication to any seller. The question of what currency is least viscous and how that relates to the legitimacy of the communication and the weighing of the medium itself consider Perek HaZahav.
  12. Notice how although the interface is always a third element, it is not always in a number three position. Keter is an interface, to the point that even En Sof Baruch Hu is a creation as is known, and Keter is number one. Kav Emtzai between yamin and smol looks like number two, with the two being extremities on either side. But don’t get confused: relationship is always third because it is preceded by two who relate. They may show up in the same instant, but the cart doesn’t go before the horse.
  13. Which is to say, in the face of Din is where you see if something is alive, because Din is the deathforce of disintegration.
  14. This is once again not anthropomorphizing because the phenomenon of want precedes the anthropic context.
  15. What is this animal, the ‘entire universe,’ that singular, living epiphenomenal entity in which we are but an organ? En Od Milvado, i.e., Retzono yitbarach, Retzono begematria Shemo.
  16. Hence ‘Medaber,’ and more accurately, not to be confused with the Kotzo Shel Yud, ‘Yisrael’ which is a totally different dimension of existence.
  17. Let’s say one lives in a world where tables are solid. In such a case, every encounter with a solid table reinforces that assumption to the point that it needn’t be checked anymore, and the data of the table’s hardness will only surface if it is somehow not as hard as one would expect. Similarly, on might live in a world where there is matter and energy, and upon learning the insight that e=mc2, is transported to a completely different universe, notwithstanding the lack of spatial locomotion. Sitting in ones seat, one can travel to worlds that are as far apart as east from west.
  18. Philosophy is in truth syntactically loaded with the idiotic worlds that suckle of the teat of its implicit legitimacy. Philosophy is in truth the original notion of a love affair (philia) with reality (sophia) that takes place in the arena of truth seeking. To directly engage with the macromodel of what the world is, whether through scientific interrogation or artistic communion, should never feel academic or dusty. It should always feel like the hot blood of life coursing through your veins because you are in touch with the heat of reality itself, with life at its core, the beating heart of the Universe Beast.
  19. On the one hand, Torat Atzilut (or in English, Systems Theory) says that since everything is a Havaya Achat, the universal is contained in every particular, and one’s home is able to capture the universal experience of being human, even though one’s home doesn’t encompass every individual’s experience. But in that very particularity, not in the universal, lies one’s unique identity. The soul of each home is particular to it alone, and that specific light that shines in the vessel of one’s family is a light that will shine no other place. What that means is that the experience next door is forever locked away, because the decision to become oneself is the decision to be nobody else. In the incision of possibility towards actualized particularity is the pernicious foil to the view from nowhere. Be nobody, and then you can have your view from nowhere, and we will all gather around to listen to your description of absolutely nothing. Or join the sighted, and be somebody who’s different vision is an addition to the conversation had by individuals.
  20. In the context of the Tzofei Edom VeYishmael that is.
